source.paraphrase: Sync subprocess calls block the loop and often run through a shell. Server code spawns async without a shell.

invariants.why: A sync call freezes the process, and a shell string lets input become commands.
invariants.fixHint: Use the async spawn or execFile variant with an argument list.
invariants.avoid: The execFile variant without a shell still blocks. Destructuring the call does not change it.

source.locator: vm is not a security boundary
source.paraphrase: The vm module runs code in a new context but is not a sandbox. Untrusted code does not go through it.

invariants.why: Context code escapes to the host process, so a string that reaches it runs with full access.
invariants.fixHint: Remove the evaluation path. Parse data with a parser instead of running it.
invariants.avoid: Compiling without running still compiles untrusted code. Creating a context alone is not this call.

source.paraphrase: exec runs the command string in a shell. Never pass unsanitized user input to it: shell metacharacters can trigger arbitrary command execution.

invariants.why: A value spliced into the command string is parsed by the shell, so a file name such as a.png; rm -rf / runs a second command.
invariants.fixHint: Call execFile or spawn with the program name and an argument array, so the value stays one argument.
invariants.avoid: Concatenation with + is the same as a template literal. A fixed command string is fine. execSync is reported by NODE-EXEC-001. exec wrapped by promisify under another name is not seen.

relations.why: createCipher or createDecipher with an ECB algorithm literal is reported by both rules.
relations.settle: Keep both: NODE-CIPHER-001 flags the removed key derivation, SA-ECB-001 the mode. createCipheriv with aes-256-gcm satisfies both.

source.paraphrase: crypto.createCipher and crypto.createDecipher are End-of-Life and removed in Node.js 22. They use MD5 without salt as the key derivation and a static IV.

invariants.why: The call throws on current Node.js, and on older versions the derived key and IV are weak, so the ciphertext is easier to break.
invariants.fixHint: Derive a key with crypto.scrypt or pbkdf2 and a random salt, then use createCipheriv or createDecipheriv with a random IV.
invariants.avoid: createCipheriv and createDecipheriv are the replacements and are allowed. Reading the function by string key is the same call.

source.paraphrase: fs.exists() is an anti-pattern because it introduces a time-of-check to time-of-use vulnerability.

invariants.why: Checking for file existence before opening or reading introduces a TOCTOU race condition where another process can delete or swap the file.
invariants.fixHint: Open, read, or write the file directly and handle errors (e.g. ENOENT) in the catch block or error callback.
invariants.avoid: Do not call fs.exists or fs.existsSync before fs.readFile or fs.open, including via destructured existsSync.
